visuals.title: Upper third: hoarse voice
visuals.text: A tumour high in the oesophagus can involve the recurrent laryngeal nerve, giving a hoarse voice.

glossary.Lower third: The bottom part of the oesophagus, nearest the stomach.
glossary.Middle third: The central part of the oesophagus, behind the heart.
glossary.Upper third: The top part of the oesophagus, in the neck and upper chest.
glossary.BMI: Body mass index: weight in kg divided by height in metres squared.
glossary.Progressive dysphagia: Swallowing difficulty that steadily worsens, typically solids first, then liquids.
glossary.Anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, meaning the blood carries less oxygen.
glossary.Metastasis: Spread of cancer from where it started to a distant site.
glossary.Malnutrition: Not getting enough nutrients, causing weight loss and weakness.
glossary.Direct access: GPs can book an endoscopy themselves without first referring to a specialist.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: cross-sectional X-ray imaging of the body.
glossary.Resection: Surgical removal of part or all of an organ.
glossary.Chemotherapy: Drugs that kill rapidly dividing cancer cells.
glossary.Radiotherapy: High-energy radiation aimed at a tumour to kill cancer cells.
glossary.Palliative: Treatment aimed at relieving symptoms rather than cure.
glossary.Unresectable: A cancer that cannot be removed surgically.
glossary.Obstruction: A blockage stopping food or fluid passing through.
glossary.Postoperative pneumonia: Chest infection after surgery, common after oesophagectomy.
glossary.Bile reflux: Backflow of bile from the duodenum up into the stomach and oesophagus.
glossary.Columnar: Tall, column-shaped cells like those lining the stomach.
glossary.Squamous epithelium: Flat, layered cells that normally line the oesophagus.
glossary.Synergistically: Working together so the combined effect is greater than the sum of each alone.
glossary.Native: The tissue normally found in that place.
glossary.Luminal: Relating to the lumen, the inside space of a tube.
glossary.Circumferentially: All the way round the wall.
glossary.Lymphatic drainage: The network of lymph vessels carrying fluid and cells from a tissue to lymph nodes.
glossary.Metaplasia-dysplasia-carcinoma sequence: Stepwise change from abnormal cell type, to disordered cells, to invasive cancer.
glossary.Tobacco: Smoking or chewing tobacco, a major cause of squamous cell carcinoma.
glossary.Lymphatic: Relating to lymph vessels and nodes.
